chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Sarin, who said:

I said to him, 'What do you say regarding staying in Mina after the people have departed?' He said: 'When he has fulfilled his ritual, let him stay as long as he wishes, and let him go wherever he wishes.'

key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj.
key_terms.نُسُكَهُ: His ritual/sacrifice, referring to the completion of Hajj rites including stoning and sacrifice.
key_terms.يَنْفِرُ النَّاسُ: The departure of the people (referring to the main exodus from Mina on the 12th or 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for staying in Mina after the pilgrims have departed?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Ash'ari and Safwan ibn Yahya, clarifies the fiqh of staying in Mina beyond the mandatory days of Tashriq. It establishes that the obligation is limited to the ritual completion, granting the pilgrim full autonomy to remain or depart, a ruling that underscores the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding Hajj logistics.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Bin Sarayy who said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the one staying at Mina after the departure of the people?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he has fulfilled his rituals, so let him stay for as long as he so desires to, and let him slaughter wherever he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from al-Hassan ibn Sariy who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who stays in Mina’ after people depart.
He (the Imam) said, ‘When he completes his acts (of al-Hajj) he can stay as long as he likes and leave as he likes.’
